question: Whose models and tools do developers actually use for agentic software work?

google.text: In a JetBrains survey of more than 15,000 professional developers (May to July 2026), as relayed by secondary trackers, the most-used tools at work were Claude Code (39%), GitHub Copilot (21%), Codex (16%) and Cursor (12%); no Google tool appears among the figures relayed.
google.label: independent-measurement

google.label: provider-claim

google.label: independent-measurement

position.label: provider-claim

position.text: StatCounter is cited as attributing about 75% of chatbot-referred page views in the United States to ChatGPT in September 2026.
position.label: independent-measurement

position.text: Anthropic sells web search as an API tool at $10 per 1,000 searches plus token costs, the same per-search price Google Cloud lists for Claude's web search on its platform.
position.label: verified-fact

assessment: On the evidence found, Google has so far absorbed the answer-engine shift inside its own product: classic search share is roughly where it was and AI Mode reached a billion monthly users about a year after launch. The exposure is economic rather than share-based, because AI answers change click and advertising behaviour, and ChatGPT is the only rival whose query volume registers. All usage figures here are secondary relays of company statements or third-party trackers.

question: Who controls the compute frontier models are trained and served on, and at what cost?

google.label: verified-fact

google.label: provider-claim

google.label: verified-fact

position.text: NVIDIA unveiled the Vera Rubin platform in January 2026, with customer availability reported from the end of September 2026; a secondary source citing Reuters puts NVIDIA at about 85% of the 2026 AI chip market.
position.label: independent-measurement

position.text: Anthropic's November 2025 commitment covers up to one gigawatt on NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems.
position.label: verified-fact

position.text: Trainium 3 is reported to have begun shipping in early 2026; coverage of Anthropic's S-1 describes a commitment of more than $100 billion over ten years to AWS for up to 5 gigawatts.
position.label: independent-measurement

position.label: independent-measurement

assessment: Google is the only frontier-model developer that designs its own accelerators, trains its own models on them and also sells the same chips to a direct rival at multi-gigawatt scale. NVIDIA still supplies the large majority of the market and every other lab, and Anthropic deliberately spreads its compute across Google, Amazon, Microsoft and NVIDIA, so the TPU agreement is diversification rather than a switch. Performance-per-dollar claims on all sides are vendor statements with no independent measurement in this dataset.
watch: When the Anthropic TPU capacity actually comes online in 2027.

assessment: Google competes in a different weight class from the leaders here: Gemma is a family of small models, while Chinese labs now publish trillion-parameter flagships under permissive or custom licences. name: Agentic commerce
question: Whose protocols and surfaces will agents use to buy things, and is anyone transacting at scale?

google.text: Google and Shopify announced the Universal Commerce Protocol on 11 January 2026; its project site is reported to list Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Salesforce and Stripe as co-developers and Visa, Mastercard, Adyen and PayPal as endorsers.
google.label: independent-measurement

google.text: Google handed the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) to the FIDO Alliance on 28 April 2026, per secondary reports.
google.label: independent-measurement

google.text: UCP checkout is reported to be launching first in the United States through Google's Universal Cart.
google.label: independent-measurement

position.text: OpenAI and Stripe released the Agentic Commerce Protocol in September 2025 to power in-chat checkout, then scaled Instant Checkout back in March 2026 so that merchants use their own checkout and ChatGPT focuses on discovery.
position.label: independent-measurement

position.text: Forrester describes US consumer adoption of Instant Checkout as low and stagnant from debut to discontinuation.
position.label: independent-measurement

position.text: Anthropic has published a marketplace experiment (Project Deal, April 2026) in which Claude bought, sold and negotiated for employees, but offers no checkout protocol of its own.
position.label: verified-fact

position.text: Amazon is listed among UCP's co-developers while running its own agent shopping features such as Buy for Me, per secondary reports.
position.label: independent-measurement

assessment: On protocols Google currently holds the stronger hand: OpenAI's in-chat checkout was scaled back within about six months, while UCP attracted rivals and card networks as backers and AP2 moved to a neutral standards body. Endorsement is not transaction volume, and no source found this cycle reports meaningful agent-completed purchase volumes for anyone. Large retailers keeping checkout on their own sites limits what any assistant can capture.
